column6: Imprinting is taught by contrast with other parent-of-origin patterns such as maternal cytoplasmic inheritance.
Imprinting is autosomal epigenetic silencing and does not draw on X-linkage.
Dosage sensitivity rests on dominance and aneuploidy, not on cis-regulatory mutation.
RAD51 strand invasion and Holliday junction resolution do not draw on mismatch repair.
Splice-site recognition and spliceosome catalysis depend on snRNA-pre-mRNA base pairing.
LCRs are built from enhancers and open chromatin, not silencers.
lncRNA mechanisms (scaffolds, guides, ceRNA) do not draw on heterochromatin spreading.
Mendelian genetics already has inherited-traits and what-is-heredity for the intuitive offspring-resemble-parents base.
miRNA biogenesis and targeting do not draw on alternative splicing.
The dependency runs the other way: the ceRNA model of lncRNAs presumes miRNAs.
MMR rests on replication errors and general DNA repair, not on BER glycosylases.
These are sibling point-mutation classes; missense/nonsense needs only the genetic code.
Barcoding is an application of sequencing; NGS platforms do not draw on it.
NHEJ is defined by contrast with homology-directed repair of double-strand breaks.
NHEJ ligates double-strand break ends; NER of UV lesions is unrelated.
Reverse dependency: overdominance is a population-genetics application of Hardy-Weinberg and selection.
PEV is heterochromatin spreading; it does not draw on silencer elements.
The topic covers Pribnow box and -35 promoter elements recognized by sigma factors.
Capping, polyadenylation and splicing do not draw on histone acetylation.
CTD coupling elaborates RNA processing; the intro topic does not need it.
RNA processing is the overview; the detailed spliceosome topic builds on it, not the reverse.
RNA processing already rests on transcription; termination detail is not needed.
miRNA biogenesis and RISC targeting do not draw on intron splicing.
Small RNA pathways do not draw on CTD phosphorylation.
Mutation rates and sources rest on dna-mutations; frameshift classification is not needed.
The end-replication problem is the lagging-strand primer that cannot be replaced at the chromosome end.
DNA recognition by binding domains does not draw on long-range enhancer looping.
Transcription factor DNA binding and activation do not draw on small RNAs.
Activation domains recruit Mediator and the initiation machinery covered there.
The topic is eukaryotic TF domains built on TFIID; sigma factors are not drawn upon.
Initiation precedes and does not draw on elongation and termination.
Translation is the RNA-to-protein step of the central dogma framed in the overview.
Elongation already has ribosomal-initiation-factors-tRNA as hard prerequisite; a second initiation link is redundant.
Cap-dependent scanning and Kozak recognition do not draw on splicing.
Unequal crossing over rests on misaligned crossing over, not nonreciprocal gene conversion.
Annotation as taught covers coding and regulatory consequences of small variants, not CNVs.
Genome-wide maps of promoters, enhancers and open chromatin presume genome organization.
GRN inference uses expression and ChIP data, not multiple sequence alignment.
Integration of molecular layers within samples does not draw on cross-species comparison.
Network-based integration methods extend regulatory network inference.

Single-cell multiome integration (RNA + ATAC) builds on scRNA-seq.
Integration rests on the omics layers listed; spatial methods are not drawn upon.
